text: The withdrawal stands and the story is written as the rework, not as the migration: RWB-P1-DM002-APP delivers the customer and party read path only, records the withdrawal of AC1 to AC3 and of TC-DM-002-01 to TC-DM-002-04 in sections 1, 2, 9 and 19, and keeps the two test case IDs with new text so the withdrawn case can be followed to its replacement. Status stays Draft (realignment v1) and no human approval is assumed.
why: R-PREC puts the FSD and TSD P1 v3, both re-based on D-RCV-35, above the legacy story master, so the migration cannot be built; but the Work Package asks for a story under this key and DP02 would otherwise have no owner, so the story is the replacement and the withdrawal must be visible rather than silent.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-002 rows Status, Decision, Why, Read path instead, Data product, Withdrawn IDs and Later home; the legacy file header lines 1-11; FSD P1 v3 change note for version 3 and A2.2; TSD P1 v3 T3.10; Template and Rules R-PREC and R6
applied_in: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 7 closing note; section 9 State transitions; section 18 Traceability; section 19 Out of scope
confirm: Recovery tech lead and the data architect when the Service Story Catalog v1 is reviewed
impact: If the programme retires the key instead, this story is withdrawn and the read path must be reassigned to a named P1 story before DP02 loses its owner; nothing in the build changes either way, because no migration is written.

text: The read path answers the customer fields of v_ace_customer, one row per contact_key of v_ace_contact with its consent and quality, one row per account of v_ace_ca_relation with its relation type, guarantee amount and guarantee date, and the four party_ext flags as one optional object; a person with no extension row is answered with the object absent and never with a default flag. The join is person_key to person_key for the three views and to party_ext, and contact_key (contact_type:key) for contact_point_ext. No column of the views is copied into rwb_source_data.
why: The replacement is given as one prose row with no answer shape, and a story cannot be built or tested against a prose row; the shape has to be fixed somewhere, and fixing it in the story keeps the field names in the dictionary and the schema rather than in code.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-002 Read path instead; FSD P1 v3 A2.1.3.2 and A2.2; TSD P1 v3 T3.3, T3.5 and T3.9

confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-source-data tech lead when the RWB-P1-E1069-APP contract is published
impact: A different answer shape changes the repository and the fixtures only; the masked identity, the no-copy rule, the 1:1 keys and the messages stay as specified.

text: The masking answer for an ACE-sourced personal field is taken from rwb-access on the authorise decision at the boundary of the caller path, as the service standard of the delivery model: this story calls the answer, applies it to the fields it returns and never writes a clear value. Because the Work Package fixes Contract dependencies as None and Patterns applied as DP05 and DP15, no C dependency and no DP-08 pattern is added; the one hop and 2 s budget of DP-11 is described in section 12.2 as the standard the story complies with and is not added to Patterns applied.
why: Architecture v5 gives the masking rows and the authorise decision to rwb-access and the application of masking to rwb-source-data, but the Work Package forbids the dependency row that the pattern table would add; leaving the boundary unstated would either duplicate the policy here or let a clear field through.

applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 8; section 7 AC3 and AC6; section 8 BR3; section 10 Authority; section 12.2; section 13 Components (MaskingClient)
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-access tech lead, before the first read is served
impact: If the plan later adds the contract dependency, only the metadata rows and the pattern table change; the behaviour of the answer is already the one described.

text: Ready to start is read from the dependency graph only, so this story may start on Day 1 although its business epic places it in wave 4: its single build edge is the platform Flyway contract RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, which is wave 0. The wave tag stays the business epic tag of EP08 and does not delay the build.
why: R5.7 rule 8 makes any story with only CON H dependencies Day 1 and the Work Package writes Day 1; a wave 4 tag on a service of wave 1 would otherwise read as a contradiction and stall a story that can be built.
read: Template and Rules R5.6 and R5.7 rules 2, 3 and 8; the service table in R4; the Work Package line for RWB-P1-DM002-APP
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 6 INVEST check; section 13 Feature switch
confirm: Programme manager when the Day-1 Work Allocation v1 is published
impact: No build change; only the sequencing note in the allocation.

text: A person_key with no row in v_ace_customer is answered as not-found, naming the key, with status 404 and nothing written: no default customer, no placeholder identity and no empty contact list. The operation that carries this answer is GET /customers/{id} of RWB-P1-E1069-APP and this story claims no path of its own; it is built from that contract's fake on Day 1, and RWB-P1-E1069-APP and RWB-P1-E1069-DB are recorded as preconditions without adding an H edge.
why: The legacy row says nothing about a key with no view row, and the case party link is a business key with no foreign key, so a key that ACE no longer holds is a reachable state; answering an empty customer would create a false record on a case screen.

impact: A different status changes the handler and the contract fixture only; the rule that nothing is written and no empty customer is returned stays.

text: The feature switch of the read path is a parameter of the platform flag library whose key and default are named by no source; the story writes them as placeholders in section 13 and reads them as data at start and per call. Off closes the read path, answers 503 with no body and reads no view, so a half-built path is never served.
why: The R-PREC default ruling puts feature flags in the platform library and the FSD describes no switch for this path; the story needs one to be deployable before the views and the grants are live, and inventing a literal key would break the rule that no business value is written in code.
read: Template and Rules R3 default rulings (feature flags) and R9; FSD P1 v3 A2.14 and A2.15; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 15
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 9 State transitions; section 13 Feature switch
confirm: Platform library owner when the Service Template Specification v1 publishes the flag key convention
impact: The key and the off behaviour change a parameter and one handler branch; the read path itself is unchanged.
